subject: Cloud Computing
title: Service Discovery
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Service Discovery.

hook.text: Service A needs to call Service B. But Service B just moved to a new server. How does A find it?

buildup.text: Service discovery is the phone book of microservices. It tracks where every service lives at any moment.

discovery.text: Cloud-native tools like Kubernetes DNS, AWS Cloud Map, and Consul handle service discovery automatically.

twist.text: Without service discovery, hardcoded addresses break whenever anything moves. And in the cloud, things move constantly.

climax.text: Service discovery is invisible when it works. When it fails, every service loses contact with everything else.

punchline.text: Services move constantly in the cloud. Discovery keeps them connected.

quiz.question: Why is service discovery essential in microservices?
options: Services frequently move to new addresses and need a way to find each other
It encrypts all communication between services
It prevents services from being deployed to the wrong region

details.summary: Service discovery allows services to find each other dynamically without hardcoded addresses. As instances scale up, down, or move, a registry tracks their current locations. Clients query the registry to find healthy endpoints.
details.whyItMatters: In cloud environments where instances are ephemeral, hardcoded addresses break constantly. Service discovery is the mechanism that makes dynamic scaling and self-healing possible.
takeaways: Services register themselves on startup and deregister on shutdown
Clients query a registry for current service locations
Enables dynamic scaling without configuration changes

faq.question: What is client-side vs server-side service discovery?
faq.answer: In client-side discovery, the client queries the registry and picks an instance. In server-side discovery, the client calls a load balancer that queries the registry. Kubernetes uses server-side discovery through its built-in DNS and service abstractions.

faq.question: What tools are used for service discovery?
faq.answer: Consul, etcd, and ZooKeeper are popular standalone service registries. Kubernetes has built-in service discovery through DNS. Cloud providers offer managed equivalents like AWS Cloud Map. Most service mesh implementations also include discovery.
